name: STAR Assurance — Kepler-equation solver audit
summary: Differential audit of elliptic Kepler solvers M -> E (hapsira, Basilisk, Orekit, star_elements) against a 40-digit truth over 8 eccentricities up to 0.9999, with probe validation on a published example and a record of what each solver does with hostile inputs.
reference: Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, Example 2-1: M = 235.4 deg, e = 0.4 -> E = 220.512074767522 deg; truth = exact inverse (mpmath, 40 digits) of the double M sent to each library
reference_observed: the printed E maps forward to M = 235.4 deg within 9e-14 deg; all 4 implementations reproduce it within 1.4e-15 rad; a synthetic Newton-from-E0=M solver diverges at e = 0.9999 and is measured, not hidden

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-06: corpus generated in-repo with mpmath, fingerprint of the rounded corpus pinned
review.G-08: subprocess only for the audited solver; inputs via stdin; runner names prefixed
review.G-13: failed run raises with stderr tail; a non-finite answer is a refusal (audit_guard); a solver failing the probe is not compared
